neighbours.label: The second word of a doubled intensifier ('really, really', 'much, much', 'very, very'); the same word used once, and doubling that is not an intensifier, stay low.
fire: Our dog was really, really sick last week.
Those new shoes look really really nice.
You owe me much, much more than that.
Her cousin got very, very lucky at the fair.
That old bridge is really, really narrow.
This job pays much, much less than mine.
These rooms get very very cold at night.
My aunt seemed really, really pleased with it.
quiet: Our dog ran and ran last week.
You owe me a lot more than that.
Her cousin got very lucky at the fair.
That old bridge is really narrow.
This job pays much less than mine.
These rooms get very cold at night.
My aunt really seemed pleased with it.

short: second word of a doubled intensifier
notes: Probes: 0.41-0.76 ('so, so' 0.28); a single ' really' 0.03-0.05, other single-intensifier sentences up to 0.20 on ' do'; other repeats ('did it and did it' 0.11, 'says, I say' 0.12) low, though the card also has ' do' x7 and ' say' x2. The model cannot see the next word, so a single use before an adjective can't read lower by what follows: the reading falls on the second copy. 12 of the top 32 peak on ' really', 5 on ' much'.
